paragraphs.en: When people {ask} me {how} I started writing, I find myself describing an {urgent} need that I felt to work with {language} .Having said that, I did {not} {know} for a long time {what} I was looking for.It was not until I followed this {feeling} {to} {its} source that I discovered I had a {passion} for writing.With some {encouragement} from my colleagues, I had one of my poems published.This {bit} of success, however, was the point where my problem began.
paragraphs.cn: 当人们 <u> 问 </u> 起我是 <u> 如何 </u> 开始写作时，我发现自己在描述一种我觉得要用 <u> 语言 </u> 来工作的 <u> 迫切 </u> 需要。话虽如此，我很长一段时间都 <u> 不知道 </u> 自己在寻求 <u> 什么 </u> 。直到我顺着这种 <u> 感觉 </u> 追溯 <u> 它的 </u> 源头，才发现自己对写作充满了 <u> 热情 </u> 。在同事的 <u> 鼓励 </u> 下，我发表了一首诗。然而，这 <u> 点 </u> 小小的成功却成了麻烦的开始。

paragraphs.en: Back in 1978, I had to {travel} between three different {campuses} in the morning, {teaching} {freshman} {composition} . {Afternoons} I spent taking my {daughter} to {her} {ballet} and {horse-riding} lessons.I {composed} my lectures on the way, and that was all the {thinking} time I had.When I {returned} home, there was not enough of me left for {writing} {after} a full {working} day.
paragraphs.cn: 早在1978年，我每天上午都要在三个不同的 <u> 校区 </u> 之间 <u> 奔波 </u> ， <u> 教大一新生作文 </u> 课。 <u> 下午 </u> 我还要送 <u> 女儿 </u> 去上 <u> 她的芭蕾 </u> 课和 <u> 马术 </u> 课。我在路上 <u> 写 </u> 讲课稿，那是我仅有的 <u> 思考 </u> 时间。 <u> 回到 </u> 家时， <u> 在 </u> 一整天的 <u> 工作后 </u> ，我已经没剩多少精力来 <u> 写作 </u> 了。

paragraphs.en: As a way {out} , I decided to {get} up two hours before my {usual} time.My {alarm} was set for 5 {o'clock} {a.m.} The first day I {shut} it {off} because I had placed it within arm's reach.The {second} day I set two {clocks} , one on my night table, and one out in the {hallway} .I had to jump out of bed and run to {silence} it before my family was {awoken} .This was when my morning writing began.
paragraphs.cn: 为了 <u> 摆脱 </u> 困境，我决定比 <u> 平时 </u> 早 <u> 起 </u> 两个小时。我的 <u> 闹钟 </u> 定在 <u> 早上 </u> 5 <u> 点钟 </u> 。第一天，我把闹钟 <u> 关 </u> 了，因为我把它放在了触手可及的地方。 <u> 第二 </u> 天，我定了两个 <u> 闹钟 </u> ，一个放在床头柜上，另一个放在 <u> 走廊 </u> 里。我不得不跳下床，在家人被 <u> 吵醒 </u> 之前跑过去 <u> 关掉 </u> 它。我的晨间写作就是从那时开始的。

paragraphs.en: Since that first morning in 1978, I have been following the habit to this day, not making or accepting many excuses for not writing.I wrote my poems in this manner for nearly ten years before my first book was published.When I decided to write a novel, I divided my two hours: the first for {poetry} , the second for fiction.Well or {badly} , I wrote at {least} two pages a day.This is how my novel, The Line of the Sun , was finished.If I had waited to have the time, I {would} still be waiting to write my novel.
paragraphs.cn: 从1978年的那个早晨开始，我就保持着这个习惯，直到今天，我不再为不写作找借口，也不接受任何借口。以这种方式写诗近十年之后，我的第一本书得以出版。当我决定写一部小说时，我把两个小时分成了两部分：第一个小时写 <u> 诗 </u> ，第二个小时写小说。无论好 <u> 坏 </u> ，我每天 <u> 至少 </u> 写两页。我的小说《 <u> 太阳 </u> 的轨迹》就是这样完成的。如果我一直等到有时间再写，那我 <u> 可能 </u> 还在等着写我的小说呢。

paragraphs.en: What I got out of getting up in the {dark} to work is the feeling that I am in control.For many people, the {initial} sense of {urgency} to create {easily} {dies} {away} because it requires making the tough decision: taking the time to create, {stealing} it from yourself if it's the only way.
